title: DC MALELE CALLS FOR INTENSIFIED FIGHT AGANIST HIV/AIDS AS LUANSHYA COMMEMORATES HTCT DAY
body_text: DC MALELE CALLS FOR INTENSIFIED FIGHT AGANIST HIV/AIDS AS LUANSHYA COMMEMORATES HTCT DAY STORY By Gideon Thole PICTURES By Berry M’tambo SATURDAY, September 5,2026 LUANSHYA District Commissioner (DC) Paul Malele has called for intensified fight against HIV/AIDS in the mining town. Mr Malele says there is urgent need to intensify the fight against the spread of HIV/AIDS with emphasis to end stigma and discrimination . He also called for an an immediate end to the current status of HIV/AIDS as a public health threat through concerted efforts. Officiating as Guest of Honour during the rescheduled Copperbelt Province official commemoration of the 2026 HIV Testing, Counselling Treatment (HTCT) Day, yesterday at Morning Market in Kamuchanga Ward, Mr Malele, said in a speech read on his behalf by Luanshya District Education Board Secretary (DEBS) Miyoba Munyumbwe Hameno, that the fight against HIV/AIDS should not be left to the Government alone. The DC called on stakeholders and health practitioners not to relent in their quest to encourage members of the public to participate in voluntary HIV/AIDS testing enmasse as a way of creating opportunities to change the approach in the fight against the disease on the local front. ” Knowing your HIV status by testing is a springboard to access treatment and address stigma and discrimination.HIV is just a disease and no one should be mocked, isolated and discriminated against because of his or her HIV status.’’ he said. Mr Malele appealed to parents and guardiansto decide the appropriate age at which to discuss with their children about sexuality related issues and the importance of seeking medicationith the virus as a way of promoting prevention of the spread of HIV/ÀIDS. The theme for this year’s HTCT Day is “One Door, Many Services: Integrated Health for a Sustainable Future.” Speaking during the same occasion, Provincial Health Director Dr Charles Mwinuna said in a speech read for him by Roan Antelope General Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Chuma Mwinga, said that Copperbelt has expanded access to HIV prevention services. Dr Mwinuna disclosed that between January and June 2026, a total of 87,411 individuals were initiated on oral prep, 1,191 Cab-la and 1,600 on injectable Lenacapavir for HIV prevention. Dr Mwinuna called on health practitioners and stakeholder on the Copperbelt to sustain the gains, close the remaining gaps and continue strengthening HIV prevention, early testing, linkage to treatment, retention in care, and viral suppression as some of the measures aimed at attaining Epidemic Control by 2030. Centre for Infectious Disease Research in Zambia (CIDRZ) regional Team Leader Dr Albert Kaonga called on the public to tak advantage of other free primary healthcare services such as male circumcision which is being being done among those who are between the ages of eight weeks up to as far as 90 years old, cervical cancer testing among females, and mental health checks which are now being given priorities. During the event Luanshya Town Clerk (TC) Collins Ndilema, was represented by District Health Director Dr Blessings Singogo ,who urged the gathering to visit health facilities which apart from offering HIV/AIDS testing now offer comprehensive health responding to growing health challenges. Health facilities have now prioritised offering: TB screening, screening for Non Communicable Diseases (NCDs), and mental health conditions. During the tour of HTCT Day exhibition stands Luanshya Mine Hospital acting administrator Sipo Kalale announced that his institution under a partnership with the Churches Health Association of (CHAZ) ,has embarked on the distribution of over 30,000 condoms pieces and 500 Self Help HIV Testing Kits to Luanshya residents. International AIDS Health Organisation –AHF Zambia, Roan Antelope General Hospital and Thompson District Hospital among other, also conducted various community engagement and provision of various of various services. The exhibitors also distributed various HIV/AIDS prevention materials to the public. In a vote of thanks District HIV/ AIDS Committee (DHAC) Representative Peter Mufwaya commended the District Commissioner, Town Clerk and stakeholders for adopting a new shift towards the promotion of collective efforts in the fight against HIV/AIDS in Luanshya. Luanshya District Administrative Officer(DAO) Kasemuka Mwalo,scores of health practitionals and residents from all walks of life also attended the HTCT Day commemoration activities. title: COUNCIL TAKES ACTION: MAPATAMATU’S REPUBLIC BAR, RESTAURANT’S CHILDREN RECREATION FACILITY CLOSED.
body_text: COUNCIL TAKES ACTION: MAPATAMATU’S REPUBLIC BAR, RESTAURANT’S CHILDREN RECREATION FACILITY CLOSED. By Gideon Thole TUESDAY, September 1, 2026. The Luanshya Municipal Council has acted swiftly and closed the children’s recreation section at The Republic, a Mapatamatu based bar and restaurant to prevent a situation where children were being exposed to anti-social behavior. Luanshya Town Clerk (TC) Collins, Ndilema, recently received a complaint from a member of the public, who raised the red flag over the happenings at the Mpatamatu based joint, directed the Council’s Departments of Public Health and Development Planning to follow up the matter and take appropriate action. Anti-social behavior is a threat to the development of good moral conduct among children compromising the future society’s moral fibre. Mr Ndilema, confirmed to this author that the complaint was found to be substantially founded. . He said children’s recreational area at The Republic Bar and Restaurant is inadequately separated from the bar and lacks dedicated sanitary facilities, raising concerns regarding the health, safety and welfare of the children. “Therefore, the children’s play area is hereby temporarily suspended pending implementation of the recommended corrective measures . The suspension applies only to the children recreational area and does not affect the wider bar and restaurant operations.” Mr Ndilema said. He added: “Failure to comply with this directive may result in the Council taking legal action, including closure of the entire premises and or revocation of the relevant license(s), in accordance with applicable legislation. A follow-up inspection will be conducted to assess compliance before the play area may resume operation.” Mr Ndilema said a report submitted to his office by a joint team of public health inspectors and town planners confirms that the premises has a designated area for children but it is has harrowing deficiencies . He emphasized that the deficiencies needs to be addressed to serve both the best interest of children and necessary legal requirements. Mr Ndilema stated that the Council findings shows that the children’s area is not adequately separated from main bar, allowing uncontrolled access between the two areas and exposing children to adults consuming alcohol. The children’s area has no dedicated toilet facilities and relies on the general bar and restaurant and further evidence documented in a video shows that children use the play area at night, raising concerns regarding their safety and supervision in a bar environment. The deficiencies also includes the fact that it has not been established whether the introduction and continued operation of a children’s recreational is compatable with the approved use of the property under applicable planning requirements. The TC said the Children’s Play Area would remain closed until the owners of The Republic Bar and Restaurant implement corrective measures prescribed by some technocrats from the local authority. Physically separate the children’s area from the bar and control access between the two areas. Providing suitable toilet facilities specifically for children using the play area. Prohibit children from using the play area at night and ensure appropriate supervision during the permitted hours. The proprietor of the Republic should engage the Council’s Development Planning Department to establish whether the children’s recreation facility is compatable with the approved use of the property, and should obtain any required approvals before the activity resumes. The Town Clerk has commended the member of the public, who reported the matter to the Council. The report among others suggested that some parents or guardians were seen consuming alcohol while the children played on the premises,during the day and night. Mr Ndilema made an assurance that Luanshya Municipal Council is committed to address all issues being brought to the attention of management by stakeholders. title: REPUBLICAN PRESIDENT INAUGURATION CEREMONY: HH CALLS FOR PEACE, UNITY, NATIONAL BUILDING
body_text: REPUBLICAN PRESIDENT INAUGURATION CEREMONY: HH CALLS FOR PEACE, UNITY, NATIONAL BUILDING By Gideon Thole TUESDAY, September 1,2026 PRESIDENT Hakainde Hichilema has pledged to continue being president for all Zambians. Speaking during the Inauguration Ceremony for the President Elect and Vice-President at the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka,the President,who has started his second term of office, following the winning of the August 13,General Election, said he is committed to serve all Zambia’s regardless of their political affiliations. In his address to thousands of people ,who included visiting foreign heads of State and Governments among other dignitaries, President Hichilema pledged to promote peace,unity and tangible development. He said politics should never reach a point where it is a matter of life and death. He thanked all the candidates who participated in the General Elections for excercsing their democratic right The President, who took the Oath of Office with his running -mate Vice President Mutale Nalumango during the ceremony, which was presided over by Chief Justice Mumba Malila, has pledged to continue the fight against corruption. During his address, the President also stressed that public servants should always put national interest above self. Some foreign Presidents and dignitaries were among the speakers, who addressed the crowd, during the colourful ceremony, attended by thousands of Zambians from all walks of life. During the momentous occasion President Hichilema was accompanied by the First Lady Madam Mutinta Hichilema. LMC PUBLIC RELATIONS UNIT. title: PUBLIC RELATIONS PRACTITIONERS URGED TO EMBRACE DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY, UPHOLD ETHICAL STANDARDS
body_text: PUBLIC RELATIONS PRACTITIONERS URGED TO EMBRACE DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY, UPHOLD ETHICAL STANDARDS By Gideon Thole TUESDAY, September 1, 2026 AN academician has called on Public Relations (PR) practitioners to embrace the use of digital technologyand uphold ethical standards in their day to day work and see to it that they were not left behind because change management is now part of various dynamic career advancement initiatives. National Institute of Public Administration (NIPA) Principal Lecturer in Public Relations and Marketing Chishimba Chishimba says it is important for PR practitioners and other communications specialists to use digital technology effectively and avoid mishandling it which can lead to negative effects such as backlashes with stakeholders. Speaking during the Closing Ceremony of the recently held, Zambia Institute of Public Relations and Communication (ZIPRC), two-day Continuous Professional Development Program on Ethics and Professional Conduct, which was held at Sandy’s Creation Resort in Lusaka, Mr Chishimba, who was the key resource person, said there was need for all PR practitioners to be well versed in the use of modern tools of communication. Mr Chishimba also urged PR practitioners drawn from the Local Authorities and other corporate bodies to uphold PR ethics’ demand for honesty and integrity when handling crisis management communication on behalf of their organisations. . He pointed out that it is important for PR practitioners to have a broad minded approach to their day to day operations ,which includes sustaining business, general service provisions and corporate communication provision. The services among others include promoting the interests of one’s employers, stakeholders and other players in the community. He further stressed that it was important for all PR practitioners to have a proactive and dynamic approach towards Government affairs ,which should be always handled well. Mr Chishimba, further reminded PR practitioners about the importance of being well versed in local and international affairs, which plays a crucial role in effectively servicing their organisations, sectors and the nation at large. And ZIPRC Acting Registrar Nasilele Mukela commended the two Ministry of Local Government Permanent Secretaries, Town Clerks and Council Secretaries for ensuring that PR and general communication services continue improving through their positive response to calls for mandatory participation in the Continuous Professional Development Programs organized by the national PR body. Ms Mukela said the Local Authorities have the largest pool of PR professionals working under the Government. Zambia is made up of 116 local authorities and each of them has its own Public Relations Unit. LMC PUBLIC RELATIONS UNIT‘ Published September 9, 2026 By Gideon Thole Categorized as Uncategorized

title: CB PS MWANZA CALLS FOR STRONGER, RESILIENT, DYNAMIC LOCAL AUTHORITIES.
body_text: CB PS MWANZA CALLS FOR STRONGER, RESILIENT, DYNAMIC LOCAL AUTHORITIES. By Gideon Thole SATURDAY, June 13, 2026 COPPERBELT Province Permanent Secretary (PS) Lawrence Mwanza has called on Local Authorities’ principal officers to ensure that they develop and sustain municipalities which are robust with capabilities to not only address the current but also anticipate future needs. Speaking during the Official Opening of the Copperbelt Province Local Authorities Principal Officers Strategic Planning Meeting, held at the Provincial Administration Conference Room in Ndola yesterday, Mr Mwanza called on principal officers to be innovative, creative and work as a team to come up with a strong support system,which will culminate into the establishment of more resilient and dynamic municipalities. The PS urged principal officers to ensure that all Local Authorities on the Copperbelt reflect the aspiration of the Government of the day, apart from ensuring that their municipalities develop into models of excellence in governance. Mr Mwanza said the Principal Officers Planning Meeting provides an important platform for both the provincial administration and Local Authorities to assess the current position, set clear priorities, and develop innovative strategies for the future. Speaking later, during the closing ceremony of the meeting, the PS urged the Local Authorities principal officers to use concerted efforts with water utility firms to find a lasting solution to issues concerning water/ sewerage systems, come up with plans of effectively implementing the 24-hours economy at district level, to act professionally, and ensure that government policy of delivering free and fair general election is realized. And speaking earlier during the same meeting, Copperbelt Provincial Local Government Officer (PLGO), Shaft Grant Musaka said Local Authorities form the foundation of communities wellbeing. Mr Musaka urged the principal officers to adopt a collective leadership approach in their quest to ensure that citizens benefit from efficient service delivery, transparent governance and sustainable development. During the meeting principal officers for Ndola, Kitwe, Mufulira, Luanshya, Chingola, Chililabombwe, Kalulushi, Lufwanyama, Masaiti and Mpongwe municipalities made submissions of completed Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects, which are ready for commissioning to the provincial administration. The principal officers shared experiences and best practices as they took turns in making presentations of their Local Authorities’ Key achievements for first and second quarters of this year. Mufulira Town Clerk Kasonde Chisanga-Musongole said the Valuation Roll has expired, CDF Loans repayment compliance has improved after taking the defaulters to court. Brand new mobile phones have been purchased and given to social cash and other community development services beneficiaries. Ms Musongole further submitted among others, that after the construction of the modern market, the Council has successfully rem been recorded in the fight against malaria as children are being provided with mosquito nets and an ambitious anti- malaria campaign which among others includes a door to door spraying covering all residential aeas. Mpongwe Council Secretary Mary Muwowo-Lapukeni stated that the Council has embarked on the construction of a modern bus station, which will contribute towards revenue collection. CDF and Cash for Work (CFW) programs are being successfully executed and political parties were having peaceful campaigns in all parts of the district, among others. Chililabombwe Town Clerk Shilla Songolo, submitted among others that the community projects were being implemented well, and various elections related issues have been resolved amicably and the change of Council motor vehicles registration from private number plates to GRZ has completed. Luanshya Town Clerk Collins Ndilema said among other that the Council has secured a nine hectares piece of land near the Maposa Electricity Sub-Power Station for the construction of two solar electricity plants under the Presidential Constituency Energy Initiative (PCEI). He said the construction of the 12 kilometres roads under the Government funded Urban Roads Rehabilitation Project has been successfully done .A new roads project covering Roan –Mpatamatu, and Fisenge areas under a Public Private Partnership(PPP) is expected to take off soon. He also said that over the past six months a total of 2,907 people have benefited from Cash For Work. Masaiti Council Secretary Wamunyima Mumbali submitted among others, that CDF and Cash For Work Projects have been successfully implemented. The transfer of Council vehicles from private number plates to Government was on course. The facilitating for the land for the land for the construction of the solar energy plants has been successfully done. Kitwe Town Clerk Patrick Kambita, who was represented by represented by Director of Housing and Social Services Field Sikanyika, said several CDF funded projects have been successfully implemented in the constituencies in the district and land for the construction of several two megawatts solar electricity production plants aimed at suppling additional power to all constituencies has been successfully identified. Kalulushi Town Clerk Betty Liswaniso said among others, that the Council has successfully implemented CDF and Cash for work projects. Various communities have continued to benefit from the health posts, classroom blocks and other public facilities which have been completed and commissioned in the past two quarters. Chingola Town Clerk Namukolo Kalufyanya said amongs,that the five percent annual budgetary allocation to finance the execution of various projects under the Ward Development Fund was being sucessfully implemented. The Government directive to change all Council vehicles registrationb from private number plates to GRZ has been successfully completed several CDF projects. The Council is currently executing several community projects under various central Government and local authority initiatives. Lufwanyama Council Secretary Mutakela Kayonde said land for the construction of the two megawatts solar electricity production plant under the PCEI has been secured and put on title. The use of five percent of the annual budget to finance the Ward Development Fund has been done and that several community projects and other CDF initiated projects have been successfully executed. Ndola Town Clerk George Mulenga said four block agriculture shows have been held in the past six months and farmers have also been empowered with inputs. A total of 16. Kilometres of roads and a total of 3.7 kilometres of drainages are expected to have a complete makeover once the on-going road rehabilitation project is completed, and a total of 32 health post have constructed under CDF. Mr Mulenga also submitted among others that Council has successfully automated revenue collection and payment systems. title: TC NDILEMA, TECHNOCRATS VISIT ROAN, LUANSHYA  PCEI POWERED CDF TWIN SOLAR PLANTS  CONSTRUCTION SITE
body_text: TC NDILEMA, TECHNOCRATS VISIT ROAN, LUANSHYA  PCEI POWERED CDF TWIN SOLAR PLANTS  CONSTRUCTION SITE By Gideon Thole & Berry M’tambo FRIDAY ,June12, 2026. LUANSHYA Town Clerk (TC) Collins Ndilema, yesterday took time to visit the 9.3 hectors piece of land which will be used to construct two solar energy power plants belonging to Roan and Luanshya constituencies under the Presidential Constituency Energy Initiative (PCEI) Project which set to take off. The proposed site is situated five kilometers from the Maposa Electricity Sub Power station, which is expected to be fed with excess power generated by the two plants which which be supplying electricity to the national power grid for onward distribution to the rest of the nation. Once operational the Luanshya and Roan solar plants are expected to produce two megawatts of electricity (2 million watts of electricity each), equivalent to four million watts, which is far beyond the electricity consumption of the entire Luanshya district. Municipal Council management recently approved the Council’s implementation of the PCEI and the use of part of Constituency Development Fund (CDF) allocations to finance solar energy plants construction by a Special Purpose Vehicle the Zambia National Energy Corporation (ZNEC). During the Management Meeting Chaired by Town Clerk Collins Ndilema, it was resolved that Luanshya Municipal Council should participate in ZNEC, and the meeting also passed a formal Management Resolution authorizing investment in to the ZNEC. The management meeting paved way for the Council’s facilitating for the implementation of the PCEI, which seek to construct two solar energy plants in Roan and Luanshya constituencies using 20 percent of this year’s CDF allocation. The Council management’s decision follows Government’s decision to develop a 312 megawatt (MV) national decentralised electricity generation progrmmme, structured at 2 MV (two million watts), electricity production plants per constituency across all the 156 constituencies in the country. The management meeting resolved to approve the construction of two twin solar energy plans,which will be situated in Maposa area in proximity to a national power substation is adjacent to the Kitwe-Ndola dual carriage highway in Luanshya. During the site visit the TC was accompanied by the Council’s Director of Development Planning Naomi Simwanza and her Administration and Human Resource counterpart Chembe Chishimba, and some specialists from the departments of development planing and engineering services. title: ECZ TIPS LUANSHYA ASPIRING CANDIDATES ON ADOPTION CERTIFICATES, NOMINATIONS PROCEDURES
body_text: ECZ TIPS LUANSHYA ASPIRING CANDIDATES ON ADOPTION CERTIFICATES, NOMINATIONS PROCEDURES STORY By Gideon Thole PICTURES By Berry M’tambo THURSDAY, May 14, 2026 The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has advised aspiring candidates in the forthcoming General Elections to ensure that they get adoption certificates from their sponsoring political parties signed by their party presidents and secretary general or president and and deputy secretary general who are registered at the Office of Registrar of Societies. And campaigns for the August 13,2026 General Elections will kick off on Friday May 29 at 06:00 hours and end on Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 18:00 hours and ECZ and all the candidates will draw a time table for campaigns for each zone. Luanshya District Electoral Officer (DEO) Collins Ndilema, said during the 2026 Elections Aspiring Candidates Briefings for Roan and Luanshya constituencies, which was held at Roan AntelopeSecondary School and Luanshya Girls Secondary School respectively, that failure to adhere to elections regulations could make a candidate disqualified. .Mr Ndilema, who is also Luanshya Town Clerk, urged aspiring candidates coming from various political pacts to use the names of their registered parent political political parties and not the names of political pacts which their parties belongs to avoid being disqualified. The mayoral, parliamentary and councilors elections aspiring candidates have also been advised to personally present and sign their nomination papers and that the use proxies during the filing nomination papers will not be allowed. The ECZ also announced that foreign national resident in Luanshya, who have residents permits and other necessary requisites are eligible contest as ward councilors. During the Aspiring Candidates Briefing, candidates were informed that Nomination Fee once paid it was non-refundable and that it is illegal for any aspiring candidate to start campaigning before officially filing in their nomination with the ECZ. Aspiring candidates, who wish to contest as independent candidates do not need any adoption certificates or any letters of introduction from any political party during the day of filing in nomination. Grade 12 of Form Five results or their equivalent for aspiring candidates can be validated by the Examinations Council of Zambia or the Zambia Qualifications Authority (ZQA)before any candidate files in their nomination papers failure to which one risk being disqualified. Aspiring candidates sponsored by political parties are required present original copies of their adoption certificates. National Assembly / Parliamentary Candidates will file their nomination papers on May 25, 2026 from 09:00 hours up to 15:00 hours. Mayoral Elections Candidates will file their nomination papers on May 26, 2026. Local Government / Ward Councillor Candidates will file their nomination papers from May 27 to May 28, 2026 from 09:00 hours to 15:00 hours. All the aspiring candidates are required to pay nomination fees through bank deposit or cash 24 hours before the nomination day. The nomination fees are as follows: PRESIDENTIAL ELECTIONS: CANDIDATES Male Candidate : K100, 000 Female Candidate : K80, 000 Youth Candidate (35 Years) : K70, 000. body_text: K24 MILLION WORTH LUANSHYA, ROAN CDF PROJECTS COMMISSIONED STORY By Gideon Thole PICTURES By Berry Mutambo SATURDAY, April 25, 2026 COPPERBELT Province Permanent Secretary (PS) Lawrence has commissioned a total of twenty-three Constituency Development fund (CDF) financed projects worth a total of K 24,184,547-00. Mr Mwanza, who was the Guest of Honour during the Multiple Luanshya and Roan Constituencies CDF Projects Commissioning Ceremony held at Fisenge Police Post, said in a speech read on his behalf, by Luanshya District Commission (DC) Paul Malele, says Government is so see to it that every Zambian has access to high standards of living through the improvement of service delivery through transparent and prudent use of CDF. The PS explained that CDF is now being used by the Government to attain equitable resources distribu way not only in Luanshya andthe Copperbelt region but the entire country. Speaking during the same event, Luanshya Mayor Charles Mulenga said the future of CDF in Luanshya was bright because it has won public trust. Dr Mulenga cited , Luanshya Dairy Cooperative founder, a Mrs Jele as a shining example of the a resident, who believe that CDF is truly transforming individual s and changing communities deserves to be supported by all. He explained that Ms Jele practically demonstrated this by donating a plot which was used for the construction of the new police station in Fisenge. The Mayor said CDF in Luanshya was being accessed by all who were vulnerable and deserve to be assisted . He said CDF has facilitated fir the accessing of techninical vocational skills by five Luanshya Correctional Facility inmates, who were about to be released and desperately in need for viable survival skills inorder to start afresh in society once they reunite with their families. Copperbelt Province Local Government Officer (PLGO) Shaft Musaka assured the gathering that the Government wants to see to it that as many deserving less privileged Zambians as possible access CDF. Mr Musaka says this is the reason why Government has continue to revise the procedures for accessingn CDF funding as a way ensuring that service delivery is improved through making the facility efficient and effective for the benefit of all Zambians Luanshya Town Clerk Collins Ndilema made an assurance that the implementation of CDF projects is heading for sustained growth and expansion. Mr Ndelima observed that CDF in the year 2022 the CDF allocation was K25 million which has been increasing year after year continuously . He noted that from the time CDF was introduced in Zambia the funds have over they ears been increased more than six times. He added that the launch of the twenty-three projects CDF Projects under the 2026 CDF allocation was a testimony of public funds being put to good use. Luanshya Constituency Development Fund Committee (CDFC) Chairperson Sherry Coleman, said over the past four and half months over K100 million has been used finance the execution of various projects in Luanshya using CDF. Professor Coleman, said the projects executed have benefited all sectors of the economy such as agriculture, health, business, energy and technology . The projects include solar powered schools, clinics. Delivering 12,000 desks, water reticulationand ablution books. Prof Coleman said between January and mid this year a total of 15 CDF financed projects, which inclued electrification of some three remote based public facilities and the Rural Electrification Authority (REA) resource allocation have been completed. The successful implemented CDF projects include the creation of four community water points in remotean and safe drinking water for the first time in forty years. Prof Coleman said Luanshya Member of Parliament (MP) Lusale Simbao and the entire CDF Committee were happy to plcrucial role in the facilitating for the execution of a total of ten brand new CDF projects worth K 12, 970,405-23. And Roan Constituency Development Fund Committee (CDFC) Chairperson Basil Mulenga, who represented area MP Joel Chibuye, ,said under the 2026 CDF aof eleven projects worth K11,214,131-77 which have been completed. Mr Mulenga said it was gratifying to continue seeing that Roan constituency economy is now steadly growing growing propelled by a series of bold residents driven development agendas that combines sustainable local development, resource utilisation,locally driven development agenda that combine sustainble local development, resource utilisation driven by opportunities and inclusive orograss Mr Mulenga added that it was heart-warming to note CDF focus is not just based on local businesses development momentum , but also a series of policy backed community driven initiatives, which are also rooted in national purpose. Fisenge resident Henry Tembo thanked the Government for taking development to the people who have been given the chance to decide the type of development they should come up with using CDF, implemented using projects submitted by residents through their area Ward Development Committees (WDCs),who later take the said projects to the CDF Committees. Mr Tembo said thanked the Government for changing the face of both urban and pre-urban areas in Luanshya, through the the provisional of additional classroom spaces ,making schools effectively providing free education. title: GOVERNMENT’S SCHOOLS FEEDING PROGRAM RECIEVES BOOST, AS  FOOD THEFTS WORRY DDCC MEMBERS
body_text: GOVERNMENT’S SCHOOLS FEEDING PROGRAM RECIEVES BOOST, AS  FOOD THEFTS WORRY DDCC MEMBERS By Gideon Thole FRIDAY, April 3, 2028 The schools feeding program in Luanshya District has received K 1.3 million financial boost from the Government which will see more food stuff added to the current lists of food given to pupils in all public schools. The District Development Coordination Committee (DDC) Meeting, which was held yesterday chaired by Luanshya Town Clerk Mr Collins Ndilema, also heard about that about Grade twelve, grade nine and grade seven 2025 national examinational schools results and the general performance of the educational sector. And the DDCC leadership also commended Heads of Government Departments (HODs) for their concerted efforts which resulted in the successful hosting of the Republican President Mr Hakainde Hichilema, who visited Luanshya on a one-day working visit last week. According to the report presented by the DDCC’s Enhancing Human Development Subcommittee, all the 89 Government owned schools in the district are carrying out the pupils feeding program. Under the program learners are feed nshima with beans and maize sample as a way of encouraging less privileged learners to attend classes, reducing cases of absenteeism maximizing the benefits and set targets of the Government’s free education program. Some DDCC members expressed concern over reported thefts of food stuff meant to feed learners under the School Feeding Program in some schools, and urged school authorities to sensitize parents in the affected areas recording thefts over the importance of initiative and urged the police to bring the culprits to book. The education sector component of the report also, among others showed that Da-Gama Special School and Hanniel Boys Boarding , (a privates school located in Fisenge area off the Luanshya –Masangano road) recorded 100 percent pass , while Luanshya Boys and Luanshya Girls which recoded 99.6 and 98.9 percent pass respectively. Rivercross Secondary School, which also act as an examination centre for grade 12 learners from Luanshya Skills Centre recorded 39 percent pass rate, lowest in the district. At grade nine level , Luanshya District was ranked number one ( produced the best passing results) in the Copperbelt Province , at Grade 12 level Luanshya was number five in the province and for grade seven Luanshya District was number seven. During the meeting, the report presented by the Human Development Committee show cased success scored in the health sector among others during the first quarter of 2026. The successes include: Recording zero maternal death in the period under review, No confirmed out breaks during the period, above target of linkage to care – above 95 percent, Health promotion activities in the district above target. Other recorded successes are::Smartcard integration at Thompson District Hospital has reduced late reporting and enhanced service delivery, Health Center Kits supply twice in facilities in the first quarter of 2026, No stock out of RDTs and HIV test kits the whole of 2025 and 2026 first quarter and Rolled out high risk clinics in 3 facilities (Mikomfwa health, Fisenge and 25 Mini hospital) among others. The DDCC’s Environmental Sustainability Committee report showed the district planned to plant 1500 pine tree seedlings in different areas in the first quarter of 2026 and so far distributed 1020 due to various challenges. The committee however, expressed hope that the exercise will be soon completed as planned. Meanwhile, a report for the Poverty and Vulnerability Reduction Sub-Committee, presented by Zambia Agency for Persons with Disabilities (ZAPD) Luanshya Coordinator Delia Nanyangwe, shows that Luanshya has 3104 disabled persons of which 900 plus suffer from physical disability and celebralpalsy. The majority of the 900 have profound and severe disabilities. According to the report, that the biggest challenge faced by persons living with disabilities in Luanshya is lack of sufficient assistive devices such as wheel chairs, clutches, walking sticks and white canes from the blind. In the first quarter of this year the Government provided a total of 24 assistive devices to Luanshya district, which included 14 wheel chairs and nine tricycles, which according to the were far from meeting the demand. During the plenary session, some DDCC members advised ZAPD to encourage its members to engage and lobby Ward Development Committee (WDC) members from their localities, Ward Councillors and their area Member of Parliament (MPs) to consider using Constituency Development Fund (CDF) to buy assistive devices for persons living with disabilities. The DDCC further dvised ZAPD and its members to take advantage of the on-going decentralization of the public service delivery by the government through the expanded CDF allocation, which is now K40 million per constituency annually. Speaking shortly before the closure of the meeting, Mr Ndilema appealed to the HODs to continue working as a team, all the time so that same zeal shown during the President’s visit should be exhibited when implementing all public programmes so that the benefits from Government services reach all corners of the District for the benefits of all without leaving anyone behind. title: NEW BUS TERMINUS COMING, AS LUANSHYA STAKEHOLDERS SUPPORT CBD TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT BY-LAW FORMULATION.
body_text: NEW BUS TERMINUS COMING, AS LUANSHYA STAKEHOLDERS SUPPORT CBD TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT BY-LAW FORMULATION. By Gideon Thole SUNDAY, March 15, 2026. THE Local Authority in Luanshya plans to build a modern bus terminus and stakeholders have agreed to support plans to formulate a new Traffic Management By-Law for the mining town. And the Luanshya Municipal Council has started holding a series of meeting with stakeholders after its management received a letter from AVIC International the Lusaka-Ndola Dual Carriage Highway, requesting the Local Authority to formulate a By-Law deterring heavy duty trucks from passing through the Central Business District (CBD). The Stakeholders Engagement Meeting was held in the Council Chamber last Friday,where Luanshya Town Ckerk Collins Ndilema, briefed the stakeholders about the contents of letter the from AVIC International. Mr Ndilema, chaired the meeting, which also discussed other developmental matters affecting Luanshya. During the Meeting, which was also attended by District Commissioner (DC) Paul Malele, who represented the District administration, the Town Clerk disclosed that Luanshya Municipal Council has now met all the conditions set to attract the World Bank’s funding under the Zambia Devolution Support Program (ZDSP), resources which would be used to construct a multi-million Kwacha worth ultra-modern bus terminus in Second Class Trading area. Others who also attended the meeting where Ward Councillors, representatives of the Bus Owners Association, Bus and Taxi Operators Association, Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA), the Zambia Police Service, the Zambia Chamber of Small and Medium Business Association (ZCSMBA) the Luanshya District Chamber of Commerce and Industry, (LDCCI) marketeers, and some Ward Development Committee (WDCs) chairpersons. During the same Engagement Meeting the Council’s Engineering Department, made a presentation, which was done by Director of Engineering Services, Engineer-Rutherford Nduli, who highlighted the need to decongest the CBD, promoting safety and securing the newly constructed roads among others by creating bypass route for trucks and other heavy duty vehicles. After a protracted debate following submissions made by LDCCI, RTSA, ZCSMBA, Zambia Police Service Traffic Division and other stakeholders the meeting resolved to support plans to formulate a Traffic Regulation By-Law,which will culminate into puting in place a bypass route. Once the By-Law is effected trucks and other heavyduty vehicles, entering and leaving Luanshya would be compelled to use a bypass route comprised of Industrial, Datura and Funyama roads connecting to Mpongwe-Masaiti and Luanshya-Ndola trunk roads (to and fro), minus passing through the CBD. And a presentation made by the Council’s Department of Legal Services, Senior Legal Assistant David-Brown Phiri, specified proposed legally binding sanctions planned to be effected by the Council, which is also the local roads authority. According to the Legal Department the Traffic Regulation By-law would affect trucks and other heavy duty vehicles carrying over 6.5 tonnes weight of cargo found passing through the CBD instead of using the bypass route. Mr Ndilema and Director of Development Planning Naomi Simwanza , also separately, assured the stakeholders that the World Bank plans to construct a bus terminus, and that they were a series of re-planning measures which the Council was now putting in place including the decongestion of the Town Centre,which among others would culminate into Luanshya Town meeting the necessary conditions to attain City status. The Town Clerk further explained , that the Council intends to embark on mass community sensitisation apart from further engaging stakeholders and interest groups as part of the Traffic Management By-Law formulation process. title: LUANSHYA CDF RESOLVES TO FUND K10 MILLION PCEI SOLAR ENERGY PLANT CONSTRUCTION.
body_text: LUANSHYA CDF RESOLVES TO FUND K10 MILLION PCEI SOLAR ENERGY PLANT CONSTRUCTION. By Gideon Thole Luanshya Constituency Development Fund Committee (CDFC) has resolved to finance the construction of a two-megawatt solar energy plant after to channeling a total K10, 090.017-13 to the project, which is aimed to addressing the problem of electricity deficit. Luanshya CDFC chairperson Professor Sherry Colemen presided over the meeting, which resolved to make adjustments to its 2026 CDF projects implementation in order to accommodate the financing for the planned construction solar electricity plant under the PCEI. Prof Coleman commended the Committee members for coming up with a unanimousresolution to accommodate the ambitious Presidential Constituency Energy Initiative solar energy plant construction project. The decision to approve the allocation of the funds to the PCEI was arrived at after the presentation of the report by the Council’s Directorate of Development Planning during the meeting. The Report among other things, stated that the Council was in receipt of the Circular issued by the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development directing each constituency to set aside Ten Million Kwacha towards the implementation of PCEI. The Luanshya Municipal Council has identified a suitable nine hectares piece of land near the Maposa national electricity grid Sub-power station, which will house both Luanshya and Roan constituencies PCEI solar energy power plants each with two megawatts (2mw) capacity. The Committee also deliberated on various issues, which also included the proposed construction of staff houses with water reticulation following the presentation of the report from Directorate of Engineering Services. The CDFC Meeting also debated on various issues affecting the wellbeing of the residents of Luanshya constituency. During the deliberations, some members of the Committee expressed concern over the urgent need for the Council to facilitate for the expediting the construction of drainages along Kamuchanga–Mwaiseni Road. They also made directives to the CDF Secretariat to carry out an investigation to validate various reports submitted by the students, who are CDF beneficiaries. The CDF secretariat was further urged to ensure that all potential skills grant beneficiaries should be advised to obtain acceptance letters from TEVETA-affiliated institutions. The Committee also gave follow-up guidance and directives to the secretariat on issues concerning 2026 grants and clubs funding and projects execution. The other issues discussed included: The of financing the successful applicants for 2026 second batch of secondary boarding schools bursary ( Form 1 and Grade 10s) was implementation following a report from the directorate of development planning. The members, who attended and participated during the deliberations of the meeting are: Bishop Morgan Kanjolo, (Vice Chairperson)\, Mr. George Mtonga ,Rev Shadrick Silungwe,Ms. Phaidessy Chisenga, Mr. Harrison Phiri,Councillor Noel Mwansa Chitenta,Councillor Austin Zimba,( who is also Deputy Mayor),Councillor Nelson Choondwe, Mr. Bernard Chansa, and Ms. Aivy K. Munyimba. Luanshya Member of Parliament (MP) Lusale Simbao and District Commissioner (DC) Paul Malele are also member of the CDFC. Luanshya Municipal Council CDF projects support staff (technocrats) from the directorates of development planning, department of finance and engineering services also attended the meeting. title: AUTHORITIES, COUNCIL MANAGEMENT, STAKEHOLDERS WELCOME NEW  LUANSHYA TC COLLINS NDILEMA
body_text: AUTHORITIES, COUNCIL MANAGEMENT, STAKEHOLDERS WELCOME NEW  LUANSHYA TC COLLINS NDILEMA STORY by Gideon Thole PICTURES By Berry Matambo MONDAY, January 5, 2026 Mayor Charles Mulenga, District Commissioner (DC) Paul Malele have welcomed newly appointed Luanshya Town Clerk (TC) Collins Ndilema, with a call for team work and enhanced stakeholder engagement. The Luanshya Mayor, who earlier met Mr Ndilema, who has taken over from Ms Sombo Kawilila, advised the new Town Clerk to adopt an open door policy apart from making sure that all stakeholders were engaged at every time of planning and executing service delivery programs. And during a Courtesy Call on the DC, the Town Clerk, who was accompanied by the Mayor, was advised to adopt the approach of a team player and ensure that the development process was not derailed but taken to a higher level. Mr Malele pointed out that Luanshya was currently recording success stories in road infrastructure development and the opening of the new mine because the leaders of the mining town were team players. In response Mr Ndilema said he was set to work with all the stakeholders in Luanshya and ensure that the Government’s developmental agenda was implemented for the benefits of all residents. Speaking earlier when he addressed members of the Luanshya Municipal Council Management, Mr Ndilema appealed the heads of Council departments to ensure that all their support staff were disciplined, focused and non-partisan in their approach to work. He urged the Council management to ensure that Government programs such as the implementation of the Integrated Development plan (IDP), Constituency Development Fund, (CDF) Cash for Work (CFW) and Devolution Support Program (DSP), were priotise and implemented accordingly without fail. The Town Clerk, who was guided by the Mayor, also check on the garbage collection and management situation in some strategic places, which among others included Second Class Trading area, Main Market in Mikomfwa and the Council dump site along the Luanshya Maserati-Mpongwe Road among others. Speaking later, when he addressed unionised employees in the Council Chamber, Mr Ndilema, -disclosed that he has over 25years’ experience in the Local Government Sector, which has seen him work in more than ten districts in different parts of the country, where he worked as a Director of Finance and Council Secretary. Mr Ndilema urged Council workers to each play their role diligently minus derailing the Government’s development agenda and service delivery. He pointed out that on all on-going Council programs such as the implementation of the Cashless Payment System, various revenue generation initiatives should continue and even get improve as a way of ensuring that the delivery of quality services to Luanshya residents was not only sustained but also improved from where his predecessor left from. Mr Ndilema,who was accompanied by the Mayor also took time to visits some stakeholders , where he farmiliarise himself with the operations of some manufacturing companies such as Emmans Farming Enterprises Ltd, which manufacture soya beans products such as cooking oil and soya cakes among others. Mr Ndilema, who once served at Mporokoso, Nchelenge and Kapiri-Mposhi Council Secretary among others was recently transferred from Kapiri-Mposhi to Luanshya by the Local Government Service Commission while his predecessor Ms Kawilila has been transferred to Livingstone. title: LUANSHYA MAYOR VISITS MIPUNDU AREA AFTER HEAVY RAINS
body_text: LUANSHYA MAYOR VISITS MIPUNDU AREA AFTER HEAVY RAINS MONDAY, December 29, 2025 His Worship the Mayor, Dr. Charles Mulenga, yesterday visited Mipundu Ward’s Chikwa area, which has been experiencing floods. The floods are caused by inadequate drainage in the area, despite the local authority installing a drainage system. The community says it’s not enough, citing refusal by some plot owners to allow the drainage system to pass through their plots, leading to diversion. The mayor assured Chikwa residents that he’ll engage engineers and planners to find a lasting solution. “We won’t let the situation persist,” he said. Mipundu Ward Councillor, Evans Mulusa, also promised to engage plot owners to discuss the issue and ensure it’s resolved. “We’ll work together to sort this out,” he said The community is hopeful that the authorities will address their concerns soon. For now, they’re calling on residents to work together with the council to find a solution. Pictures by Berry M’tambo LMC PUBLIC RELATIONS UNI Published December 31, 2025 By Gideon Thole Categorized as Uncategorized
